Increase the font weight only.
Remove all headings.

questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: narrower columns shorten line length and reduce fatigue. On that basis "Split text into narrower columns" is the supported choice. questions.learningObjective: Recognise when colour is used decoratively rather than functionally.

stimulus.body: A short reference note on colour as emphasis is set for a close-reading task. It states: Colouring a heading just for appearance is decorative. A marginal reminder adds: colour should serve a function. Four statements are then offered, and only one of them follows from what the note actually says.

questions.stem: Testing “Recognise when colour is used decoratively rather than functionally. / Colour should serve a function. / Colour as emphasis” against the excerpt, which option is the defensible one?

options.text: Colour coding bus routes on a map.
Colouring a key figure in a table.
Colouring a heading because it looks nice.
Colouring a warning in red.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: colouring a heading just for appearance is decorative. On that basis "Colouring a heading because it looks nice" is the supported choice. Option A ("Colour coding bus routes on a map") fails because it treats functional coding as decoration; Option B ("Colouring a key figure in a table") fails because it treats emphasis as decoration; Option D ("Colouring a warning in red") fails because it treats signalling as decoration.
